Let $G$ be an infinite weighted graph on a countable vertex set $X$ with symmetric edge weights and a vertex measure. Its Laplacian, defined on finitely supported functions $C_c(X)$ in $\ell^2(X,m)$, is known to be essentially self-adjoint, so it has exactly one self-adjoint extension in $\ell^2(X,m)$.
Does this Laplacian necessarily exhibit Markovian uniqueness? (Yes/No)

question:
Let $G$ be an infinite, locally finite weighted graph on the vertex set $\mathbb{N}$, with edges only between consecutive integers $n$ and $n+1$. Equip $G$ with a path metric under which $G$ is a complete metric space, and this metric is of the kind covered by the completeness criteria for uniqueness of extensions of the graph Laplacian.
Is the Laplacian on $G$ guaranteed to exhibit Markovian uniqueness? (Yes/No)
atom_statement: Completeness of the graph $G$ with respect to particular choices of path metrics is sufficient for Markovian uniqueness.
evidence: In particular, completeness of G (with respect to particular choices of path metrics) is sufficient for the Markovian uniqueness.

question:
A weighted metric graph has countably many edges $e_1, e_2, \dots$ and infinite intrinsic size. Starting from a given model, we cut $e_1$ into equally short pieces, then cut $e_2$ into even shorter equal pieces, then cut $e_3$ into still shorter equal pieces, and so on through all the edges one after another. The result is a refined model of the same graph.
Can this procedure produce a refined model whose essential intrinsic size $\eta^*_{\rm ess}$ equals $0$? (Yes/No)
atom_statement: For any model, one can obtain a refined model with $\eta^*_{\rm ess}=0$ by cutting edges into equally short pieces, taking the countably many edges one after another and cutting each successive edge into shorter pieces, which works even if the weighted metric graph has infinite intrinsic size.

Indeed, for each model the edge set E is countable and hence one can obtain a new model satisfying ess.zE/ D 0 by “cutting” an edge into equally short pieces; then the next edge into shorter ones, and so on.

question:
Let $(\mathcal{G},\mu,\nu)$ be a weighted metric graph with Dirichlet Laplacian $\mathbf{H}_D$. Under which condition is the heat semigroup $(e^{-tH_D})_{t>0}$ recurrent?
A) Exactly when the discrete-time random walk on the set of edges, rather than on the vertex set $\mathcal{V}$, is recurrent for some (equivalently, every) simple model of the graph.
B) Exactly when the discrete-time random walk on the vertex set $\mathcal{V}$ with transition probabilities $P=(p(u,v))$ is recurrent for some (equivalently, every) simple model of the graph.
C) Exactly when the discrete-time random walk on the vertex set $\mathcal{V}$ with transition probabilities $P=(p(u,v))$ is recurrent for some simple model of the graph, while for other simple models the walk may be transient.
D) Exactly when the discrete-time random walk on the vertex set $\mathcal{V}$ with transition probabilities $P=(p(u,v))$ is transient for some (equivalently, every) simple model of the graph.
atom_statement: For a weighted metric graph $(\mathcal{G},\mu,\nu)$, the heat semigroup $(e^{-tH_D})_{t>0}$ generated by the Dirichlet Laplacian $\mathbf{H}_D$ is recurrent if and only if, for some (and hence for all) simple model of the graph, the discrete-time random walk on the vertex set $\mathcal{V}$ with transition probabilities $P=(p(u,v))_{u,v\in\mathcal{V}}$ is recurrent.

question:
Consider the Dirichlet form $\mathfrak t[u]=\int_{\mathbb R}|u'|^2\,dx$ on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ with domain $H^1(\mathbb R)$. question:
On the Hilbert space $L^2(0,1)$, consider a quadratic form $\mathfrak t$ with a linear domain $\mathrm{dom}(\mathfrak t)$ that is a proper closed subspace of $L^2(0,1)$ (so not dense). The form $\mathfrak t$ is non-negative and Markovian. Is $\mathfrak t$ a Dirichlet form in the wide sense? (Yes/No)
